clue.text: Firm I didn't buy out?

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters of the phrase are rearranged

parts.note: someone who didn't buy, but parted with goods, sold them

explanation.surface: A shopper remarks that they left a company's shares alone during a buyout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I didn't buy' reads as I SOLD; 'out' rearranges those five letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something solid is firm and unyielding, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: The form Mr Quelch had to take away

definitions.meaning: Mr Quelch is the schoolmaster in the Billy Bunter stories
to take away is to lift something off and shift it elsewhere

explanation.walkthrough: In some British public schools a form (class) is called the Remove; Mr Quelch teaches the Remove in Frank Richards's Greyfriars stories.
explanation.definitionFit: Quelch's class at Greyfriars bears this name, and to take something away is to shift it off, a verb synonym.

clue.text: He called out the name of a little place on the Thames

definitions.text: He called out the name of a little place on the Thames

parts.words: He called out the name of a little place on the Thames
parts.note: pictures a railway porter shouting a station name: the station is a small Gloucestershire town on the upper Thames

explanation.walkthrough: Lechlade is a small town in Gloucestershire near the source of the Thames, once on a branch railway line.
explanation.definitionFit: Lechlade is a small riverside town at the head of the navigable Thames.

clue.text: US soldier breaking into a London gallery to stir up public feeling

indicators.note: breaking into says one piece forces its way inside another

parts.note: the Tate is a famous art gallery in London
GI is the usual name for an American soldier

explanation.surface: An American serviceman bursts into a London art gallery to rouse public opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking into' puts the soldier between the article and the gallery's name.
explanation.definitionFit: To agitate is to campaign so as to arouse public concern, a direct synonym.

clue.text: A museum piece to be looked into?

definitions.text: A museum piece to be looked into?

parts.words: A museum piece to be looked into?
parts.note: a 'museum piece' sounds like an exhibit, but this is the glass cabinet one peers into

explanation.definitionFit: A glass-fronted display cabinet in a museum is something visitors gaze into.

clue.text: Old-fashioned lovers describing a baby-carriage belonging to us?

indicators.note: describing in its sense of drawing a line round, so one piece encircles another

parts.note: a pram is a baby-carriage
belonging to us means ours

explanation.surface: Someone describes a pram that the family owns, in the manner of dated romances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describing' is used in its geometric sense of drawing round, so the baby-carriage goes round the article.
explanation.definitionFit: Paramour is a dated word for a lover, often an illicit one.

clue.text: Valuable old coin given to Eros in error

indicators.note: in error means mistakenly, so the letters are placed wrongly and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A precious antique coin has been handed to the statue of Eros by mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram is of GIVEN and EROS together; 'to' is a link. Eros is the statue at Piccadilly Circus in London.
explanation.definitionFit: A British gold coin worth a pound, now chiefly a collector's piece.

clue.text: Fiddle the account he will if he gets a chance!

definitions.text: Fiddle the account he will if he gets a chance!

parts.words: Fiddle the account he will if he gets a chance!
parts.note: the whole clue describes a dishonest person who will fiddle the books whenever possible; fiddle is the verb, and the rogue is also named by it

explanation.definitionFit: To fiddle accounts is to defraud, and a dishonest person who does so is a swindler.

clue.text: Cook too much fish?

definitions.meaning: to scorch or blacken food by overcooking
a freshwater fish of the salmon family found in cold lakes

explanation.definitionFit: Overcooked food is burnt black on the outside, and the Arctic species is a trout-like fish.

clue.text: A shot that comes off?

parts.note: 'comes off' suggests a successful shot, but read as a bullet that glances off a surface

explanation.definitionFit: A rebounding bullet or stone bounces off a hard surface.

clue.text: Commodious back seat on a Jumbo

definitions.text: Commodious back seat on a Jumbo

parts.words: Commodious back seat on a Jumbo
parts.note: a Jumbo suggests a jumbo jet, but here it is an elephant, and the seat rides on its back

explanation.walkthrough: Jumbo is a stock name for an elephant (after a famous London Zoo elephant), not the jet.
explanation.definitionFit: A canopied seat carried on an elephant's back, used in India.

clue.text: The Greek character from whose gaze Tantalus shrank

indicators.note: from shows the letters are taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A mythological figure flinches from the stare of a Greek hero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' takes the run of letters across 'gaZE TAntalus'; 'character' means a letter, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: The sixth letter of the Greek alphabet, a character in the written sense.

clue.text: Arrogant sort of vinegar

indicators.note: sort of here means a rearranged version of the word, as in sorting letters

explanation.surface: A haughty kind of vinegar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of' reads as a description of the vinegar but signals the anagram of ARROGANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Vinegar flavoured with this herb is a common kitchen variety, so the herb names the vinegar type.

clue.text: Thanks to natural evolution, it has a maddening bite

parts.note: ta is British informal for thanks

indicators.note: evolution means change of form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Natural selection explains why some creature's bite drives people mad.
explanation.walkthrough: Its bite was once believed to cause tarantism, a frenzied dancing mania.
explanation.definitionFit: This large hairy spider's bite was thought in Italy to cause a dancing madness.

clue.text: Noxious herb we were very angry about

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word wraps round the other

parts.note: raged means were very angry

explanation.surface: We were furious about a poisonous weed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' means the verb wraps round the pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: A yellow-flowered weed poisonous to livestock, hence noxious.

clue.text: What male Caucasians are when a piece of news is brought in?

indicators.note: brought in says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: an item is a piece of news in a paper

explanation.surface: Asks what pale-skinned men are when a news report arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought in' means the piece of news goes inside the clue's own word 'when'.
explanation.definitionFit: Caucasian means of European descent, pale-skinned; males so described are pale-skinned males.

clue.text: Elongated fruit about which a footnote is published

indicators.note: about means going round, so the footnote phrase wraps round the fruit

parts.note: PS, postscript, is a note added at the end
a pear is a fruit longer than it is wide

explanation.surface: A pear-shaped fruit gets a note at the foot of the page when it comes out in print.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' means the article and the postscript go round the fruit; 'which' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A book that comes out in print is said to come out, a synonym.

clue.text: Public relations for a range of items such as sugared almonds

parts.note: a shop's lines are its ranges of goods

explanation.surface: A publicist promotes a range of confectionery like sugared almonds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' and 'such as' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: These confections are nuts coated in caramelised sugar.

clue.text: A seize up in an offer that's too good to be missed

definitions.text: an offer that's too good to be missed

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to grab is to seize

explanation.surface: Getting stuck in a deal too good to miss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seize up' looks like jamming, but 'up' (in a down clue) turns the synonym for seize, and the clue's 'A' and 'in' follow as written.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheap purchase is a deal one should not pass up.

clue.text: A tomb in a newly developed part of Canada

indicators.note: newly developed means remade, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grave is found in a recently settled region of Canada.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram uses all eight letters of 'A tomb in a'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Canadian prairie province.

clue.text: Has no rent to worry about?

definitions.text: Has no rent to worry about?

parts.words: Has no rent to worry about?
parts.note: someone with no rent to pay is a householder with the property outright

explanation.definitionFit: A person who possesses their home outright pays no landlord.

clue.text: A shot person's dreadful colour?

parts.note: a shy is a throw or shot, as at a coconut shy

explanation.surface: Someone turns a ghastly colour on seeing a gunshot.
explanation.walkthrough: A coconut shy is a British fairground stall where one throws balls at coconuts.
explanation.definitionFit: A grey, ashen pallor is the colour of someone in shock.

clue.text: Light cavalryman mounting without thinking about us .

indicators.note: about means going round, so the reversed word wraps round the second piece
mounting means rising, which in a down clue reads the word upwards

parts.note: rash means acting without thinking

explanation.surface: A cavalryman leaps into the saddle heedlessly, with no thought for us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounting' turns the word for heedless upwards in this down clue, and 'about' wraps it round the clue's 'us'.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of a light cavalry regiment, originally Hungarian.

clue.text: Take a horse south on forest roads

parts.note: to ride is to go on horseback

explanation.surface: Riding south along woodland tracks.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a ride is a broad track cut through woodland for horse riders.
explanation.definitionFit: Woodland tracks cleared for horse traffic are called by this name.

clue.text: What the gravel was over the street Wren redesigned?

indicators.note: redesigned means rearranged, as an architect might replan a building

explanation.surface: Gravel scattered on a road that Christopher Wren replanned.
explanation.walkthrough: Wren is the architect Sir Christopher Wren; his name is rearranged after ST.
explanation.definitionFit: Gravel spread across a surface is scattered over it.

clue.text: Gets help, though it's clearly denied

parts.note: gains means gets
aid means help

explanation.surface: Someone receives assistance, though they plainly refused it.
explanation.definitionFit: To contradict or deny a claim is an old-fashioned sense of this verb.

clue.text: Fifty odd deer gathered round flowering tree

indicators.note: gathered round means surrounding, so the rearranged letters wrap round the numeral
odd means peculiar, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: About fifty strange deer cluster round a tree in blossom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' rearranges DEER to EDER, which is 'gathered round' L.
explanation.definitionFit: A small tree bearing white flower clusters and dark berries.

clue.text: Apprentice I vigorously chided after release from detention?

parts.note: L, for learner, stands for an apprentice
berated means scolded vigorously

explanation.surface: A trainee was told off sharply on getting out of detention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' belongs to the definition: freed is what one is after release.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone freed from custody has been set free.
